Aug 27 Block Heatmaps

Per-condition heatmaps of block darkening over time: three magnet repeats against their three controls, one condition per panel. Gap (injection) side is on the left of every cell, magnet side on the right.

How to read: each panel is one condition, two rows: magnet arm (top) and no-magnet controls (bottom), each cell the mean of the 3 repeats; columns are five time stages. Every cell is the agarose block from above; the white dashed line is the gap/block boundary measured at t = 0 (right edge of the NP reservoir), held fixed for later frames — agarose shrinkage is shown, not compensated. The x-axis is calibrated per series: boundary → block right face = 10 mm; the sliver left of the line is the injection gap (reservoir). Processing (validated frame-by-frame against photos on 0.4 non-BSA COOH magnet r2): frames ECC-registered onto their series’ t = 0, anchored at the gap’s left edge, one crop per series; color = absolute NP darkness minus each frame’s own gel-interior floor (exposure cancels), median-binned and lightly smoothed; one shared color scale (0–22 L*). Caveats: in magnet rows the magnet’s shadow adds some signal toward the right and deepens with ambient-light changes (12 h shots were at night); occasional residual edge slivers come from frames whose alignment is imperfect. Per-repeat kymographs and the analyses are on the companion pages.
